brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full plus piece:0,1,0;half-n, bolted together (jointBolt:0#0,0#5), with caps on the open sides
bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-half-div3 (3 compartments) and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-half-n-half-div2 (2 compartments). They drop in and hang on their rims with no fixings, so they lift out once the top cover is off.
drawer:0#0,1#cut on the cut face of the half base
handle:0,0,0;top on the top cover of the full cell (cover:0,0,0;full;top), with its inserts. The configurator checks fit only, not how much weight the handle can carry.
It's a compact two-cell, closed unit with a handle on top. Whether it holds up when carried full depends on the print material and strength, which the configurator doesn't check.

finish.summary: I built a compact, closed electronics organizer from two cells: a full hex base and a north-half base with a drawer on its cut face. Two drop-in bins with dividers sit under top covers, and a carry handle is fixed to the full cell's cover. I capped the open faces and bolted the joint, which brings it to 29 parts. check_build passes with no rule errors and meshClash "clear". I dressed it with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs in the bins and tweezers in the drawer. The screws, nuts and standoffs are hidden under the covers in normal views, as you'd expect in a closed case. I didn't add props to every bin compartment, and the drawer's other compartments are empty because the parts props didn't fit them.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
